problem: Cookies spread too thin and flat
likelyCauses: Butter was too soft or melted when creamed
Too little flour relative to fat and sugar
corrections: Chill the dough at least 30-60 minutes before baking
Start with butter that's cool but pliable, not soft or melted
Double-check flour measurement -- spoon and level rather than scooping directly from the bag

problem: Cookies came out cakey instead of chewy or crisp
likelyCauses: Too much flour relative to fat
Overmixed after adding flour, developing too much gluten
corrections: Measure flour by weight if possible, or spoon-and-level if by volume
Mix just until the flour disappears, not longer
Check the leavening amount against the recipe -- it's easy to double it by mistake

problem: Cookies are dry or crumbly when that's not the intended texture
likelyCauses: Not enough fat or liquid binder
corrections: Pull cookies when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone -- they finish cooking on the hot pan
Confirm the fat/egg amounts match the recipe

problem: Cookies didn't spread at all and stayed as mounded balls
likelyCauses: Dough was overchilled and baked straight from the freezer without adjustment
Not enough fat or sugar relative to flour
corrections: Let overchilled dough sit a few minutes at room temperature before baking, or add a minute or two to the bake time
Confirm butter/sugar amounts match the recipe

problem: Cookies look pale and underbaked even after the recipe's stated bake time
likelyCauses: Oven temperature running cooler than the dial says
Dough was too cold going in, extending real bake time
Sheet pan is a lighter color and reflects rather than absorbs heat
corrections: Verify actual oven temperature with a separate oven thermometer
Add a minute or two rather than assuming the recipe's timing is wrong
Darker pans bake faster than light or insulated ones -- adjust time accordingly

problem: Bottoms burn before the tops finish baking
likelyCauses: Baking on a dark or very thin pan without a liner
Rack positioned too low in the oven
Oven running hotter than the dial indicates
corrections: Use parchment paper or a silicone mat as a buffer layer
Move the rack to the middle of the oven
Verify actual oven temperature with a separate oven thermometer
